title: Stocking Any Material
short_answer: Put material in the room where it gets used — not by the door, not in one big pile. Every extra carry is time nobody paid for.
summary: Stocking looks like the cheapest task on the job, so it gets the least planning. That is exactly why it quietly sets the labor cost of every stage after it.
plain_words: Put the material in the room where it gets used. Not by the door, not in one big pile. Every time somebody has to pick a thing up and move it again, that is time nobody paid for.
when_to_use: Before any delivery is scheduled — all trades
Closing out a job with returnable overage
prerequisites: Room-by-room or zone staging plan — not "the third floor"
GC coordination on access, floor loading, and weather-tight storage

tools.name: Tarps or covers for weather-sensitive material

steps.title: Landing location
steps.body: Confirm where it lands, by floor and by room — not "the third floor."

steps.title: Access
steps.body: Confirm gate hours, delivery window, dock, hoist or elevator reservation, and who has the key.

steps.title: Route
steps.body: Confirm the route is still open — a corridor framed since you last walked it kills a delivery.

steps.title: Floor loading
steps.body: Confirm floor loading with the GC before staging heavy material on a suspended slab. Structural question, not a convenience question.

steps.title: Weather-tight
steps.body: Confirm the area is weather-tight if the material cannot get wet.

steps.title: Receiver
steps.body: Confirm who receives, counts, and signs.

steps.title: Placement
steps.body: In the room it gets used in, or the closest space that is not a work surface.

steps.title: Do not block
steps.body: Never block egress, exit doors, electrical panels, extinguishers, sprinkler risers, or another trade's active work.

steps.title: Spread weight
steps.body: Spread the weight. Get it off a slab that could be wet — sleepers, dunnage, pallets. Cover what needs covering.

steps.title: Count at truck
steps.body: Count it against the order before the driver leaves. A shortage found tomorrow is our shortage.

steps.title: Reject damage
steps.body: Inspect and reject damaged material at the truck. Note shortages and damage on the ticket before signing.

steps.title: Photo and ticket
steps.body: Photograph the load in place. Send the ticket to the office same day.

steps.title: Track overage
steps.body: Returnable material is real money — count it and call it in before the return window closes.

steps.title: Consolidate scrap
steps.body: Consolidate scrap early. Scrap collected as you go costs a fraction of scrap collected at the end.

steps.title: Feedback to estimating
steps.body: Report actual vs ordered back to the estimator in plain numbers.

warnings.title: Timing
warnings.body: Too early is the more expensive mistake — material gets damaged, stolen, blocks trades, and gets handled extra times. Too late stops a crew cold. Target: just far enough ahead that the crew never waits, and no further. Stage in waves on long jobs.

warnings.title: Why the photo matters
warnings.body: A dated photo of material staged and undamaged settles whether the supplier shorted us and whether another trade damaged our material after we set it. Neither is winnable from memory.

quality_checks.prompt: Material staged in the room or zone where it will be installed
Count and damage notes completed before the driver leaves
Dated photo and ticket to office same day
Nothing blocks egress, panels, or another trade's active work

common_mistakes.title: One pile per floor
common_mistakes.wrong: Drop everything at the elevator landing
common_mistakes.right: Split by room or zone from the plan
common_mistakes.why: Every extra carry is unpaid labor

common_mistakes.title: Too early delivery
common_mistakes.right: Wave deliveries days ahead of the crew

common_mistakes.title: Unsigned shortage
common_mistakes.wrong: Sign the ticket with a shortage and hope the office fixes it
common_mistakes.right: Note shortages on the ticket before signing

provenance.note: General construction material-handling practice plus GVC field experience. Receiving and documentation steps protect against supplier shortages and cross-trade damage claims. Floor-loading coordination is a life-safety item — always the GC's and structural engineer's call.
